title: Colombia vs. Mexico vs. Chiang Mai: A 2026 Cost-of-Living and Visa Breakdown for Non-US Remote Business Owners

# Colombia vs. Mexico vs. Chiang Mai: A 2026 Cost-of-Living and Visa Breakdown for Non-US Remote Business Owners

If you run a U.S. LLC from abroad and want to keep overhead low without sacrificing quality of life, three destinations dominate the conversation: Medellín, Mexico City, and Chiang Mai. Here is exactly what each one costs, how the visas work, and which type of remote operator each city actually suits.

---

## The Monthly Cost Comparison at a Glance

All figures below reflect a mid-range digital nomad lifestyle: private accommodation, coworking access, decent food, occasional travel within the country, and health insurance.

| Expense | Medellín, Colombia | Mexico City, Mexico | Chiang Mai, Thailand |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rent (1BR, central) | $600 to $900 | $800 to $1,200 | $350 to $600 |
| Coworking (monthly) | $80 to $150 | $150 to $250 | $60 to $120 |
| Food (eating out daily) | $250 to $400 | $300 to $450 | $150 to $250 |
| Transport | $30 to $60 | $40 to $80 | $40 to $80 |
| Health Insurance | $80 to $150 | $100 to $180 | $60 to $120 |
| **Total Monthly Est.** | **$1,040 to $1,660** | **$1,390 to $2,160** | **$660 to $1,170** |

> Note: These figures assume you are paying as a foreign national without local subsidies. Costs in Medellín and Chiang Mai have risen steadily since 2023 due to increased nomad demand, but both still represent strong value against Western Europe or North America.

---

## Visa Reality in 2026

### Medellín, Colombia

Colombia remains one of the most accessible countries for remote workers. As of 2026, you can enter visa-free for up to 90 days (extendable to 180 days per calendar year) on most Western and Latin American passports.

For longer stays, the **Digital Nomad Visa (Nómada Digital)** is the most relevant option. Requirements include:

- Proof of remote income of at least 3x Colombia's minimum monthly wage. The 2026 minimum wage is COP 1,750,905, which converts to approximately $467 to $480 USD per month, or roughly $540 to $550 USD when including the mandatory transport subsidy. Your income threshold will be calculated against the official COP figure.
- A valid U.S. LLC or foreign business entity counts as your income source
- Application submitted to the Colombian Migration Authority online
- Visa validity: up to 2 years

On renewal: the visa is technically renewable, but you should proceed with caution. There are credible reports from immigration attorneys that Colombia may currently be denying consecutive renewals in practice. Treat renewal as uncertain rather than guaranteed, and have a contingency plan ready.

Processing time is typically 4 to 6 weeks. The application fee is around $50 USD.

### Mexico City, Mexico

Mexico operates on a tourist permit system, not a traditional tourist visa. On arrival, most nationalities receive a **180-day tourist permit (FMM)**, one of the most generous in the world.

There is no dedicated digital nomad visa in Mexico as of 2026. Your realistic long-term options are:

- **Temporary Resident Visa:** Requires proof of monthly income of approximately $4,200 to $4,500 USD over the last 6 months, or savings and investments averaging approximately $70,000 to $74,000 USD over the last 12 months. Valid for 1 to 4 years.
- **Renewal via border run:** Technically possible but increasingly scrutinised by immigration officers. Do not rely on this as a long-term strategy.

The income and savings thresholds for the Temporary Resident Visa are significantly higher than Colombia's, which makes Mexico better suited to operators with stronger, well-documented revenue.

### Chiang Mai, Thailand

Thailand's visa situation is the most dynamic of the three. The **Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa**, introduced in 2022, remains active in 2026 and is the gold standard for remote workers earning over $80,000 USD annually. It offers:

- 10-year renewable stay
- Full exemption from Thai personal income tax on foreign-sourced income remitted to Thailand, under Royal Decree No. 743
- Fast-track immigration and other perks

For those below the income threshold, the most common strategy is a combination of tourist visas and TR extension arrangements through Thai immigration. The **Thailand Elite Visa** (now called the **Thailand Privilege Card**) starts at approximately 650,000 THB (roughly $18,700 to $19,000 USD) for the entry-level 5-year Bronze tier, and remains popular among serious long-term residents.

Budget-focused nomads most commonly use 60-day tourist visas with single extensions, cycling every 3 to 4 months.

> Note: If your U.S. LLC generates income in Thailand, you need to understand Thailand's territorial tax rules carefully. Foreign-sourced income remitted in the same year it is earned became taxable in Thailand from 2024 onward. Consult a tax professional before committing to long-term Thai residency.

---

## Which City Fits Which Operator?

| Profile | Best Fit |
|---|---|
| Early-stage operator, budget under $1,500/month | Chiang Mai |
| Spanish speaker or Latin America-focused business | Medellín |
| Networking-heavy, startup-adjacent business | Mexico City |
| High earner seeking long-term visa stability | Chiang Mai (LTR) |
| Wants 1 to 2 year flexibility without heavy paperwork | Medellín |

---

## The U.S. LLC Angle

All three cities have robust coworking scenes and reliable high-speed internet. Running a U.S. LLC from any of them is entirely feasible. Your LLC remains a U.S. entity regardless of where you live, which means your banking, compliance, and payment processing stays intact.

If you have not yet formed your LLC or you want to make sure your structure is set up correctly for operating abroad, start with our [LLC Guide](/llc-guide) or book a session through our [Consultancy](/consultancy).
